summary: The fix correctly prefers the upstream tracking branch (via `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{upstream}`, stripping only the remote-name prefix) over the local checked-out HEAD name when resolving the branch to persist to task.yaml, falling back to the prior local-HEAD behavior when no upstream is configured; both subprocess calls avoid shell=True and use list-form args so there is no injection risk, the upstream lookup omits check=True (its failure is an expected, handled branch) while the fallback keeps check=True as before, and I independently verified via a scratch git repo that --symbolic-full-name/--abbrev-ref together produce the same 'origin/branch' output being parsed and that the split("/", 1) logic correctly preserves slashes inside the real branch name. All three tests (including the two pre-existing ones) pass locally against the real veridian-task.py module rather than a reimplementation. The diff is purely additive (script logic + new regression test), touches no migrations/SQL/auth/permission/billing/security paths and no .github/workflows/** files, matching its tier1 classification.
issues: Minor, non-blocking edge case: if a branch's upstream is itself a local branch (not a remote-tracking ref) whose name happens to contain a '/', the blind `split("/", 1)[1]` strips what looks like a remote prefix but is actually part of the branch name, e.g. upstream 'other/branch' would be mis-parsed to 'branch'. Not reachable via this repo's actual workflow (workers only track real remote branches, always via 'origin/...'), so it doesn't block approval, but worth a code comment or a `git config branch.<name>.remote`-based check if local-to-local tracking is ever introduced.
